name: Golden Gate Park
start_event: Park Act signed 4 Apr 1870 by state legislature; site surveyed by W.H. Hall 1870
planting_note: Dune reclamation began 1871 at east end (270 ac incl. Panhandle); 22,000 trees set out 1872, ~60,000 by 1875, 155,000 by 1879; ~600 ac west of Strawberry Hill forested later (Monterey pine/cypress, blue gum); largely mature by 1890; west end finished c.1900 (Beach Chalet 1900, windmills 1902-08)

name: Lake Merced Park
start_event: Officially designated a park run by Rec & Park in 1950 (city bought lake from Spring Valley Water Co. 1930)
planting_note: Harding Park golf course developed on leased Spring Valley land in 1920s; tracts near the lake forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: John McLaren Park
start_event: Supervisors voted 1926 to buy 550 ac; dedicated with tree-planting ceremony Dec 1927; land assembled 1928-46 (SNRAMP says dedicated 1934)
planting_note: Dedication tree planting 1927; WPA scenic drive and landscaping 1930s; most facilities built 1950-80; 2,290 seedlings planted 1965-66

name: San Francisco Zoo
start_event: Fleishhacker Zoo founded 1929 beside Fleishhacker Pool (1925) and playfield
planting_note: First exhibits and landscaping built 1930s (WPA)

name: Lincoln Park
start_event: Former city Golden Gate Cemetery (1868) turned over to Park Commission 1909; graves relocated
planting_note: Golf 3 holes 1902, 14 by 1914, 18 by 1917; Legion of Honor 1924; tract forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: Yacht Harbor and Marina Green
start_event: Yacht Harbor and North Gardens (now Marina Green) built for 1915 PPIE and acquired by city from the Exposition
planting_note: Green is lawn on PPIE fill; Montgomery/Marina airfield use from 1920; Gas House Cove bought 1939-49, harbor expanded mid-1960s

name: Glen Canyon Park
start_event: City purchased 101-ac canyon from Crocker Real Estate Co. 1922
planting_note: Blue gum windbreak from Sutro's 'Gum Tree Ranch' era; recreation center at south end (WPA era)

name: Crocker Amazon Playground
start_event: Recreation Commission given permission 1934 to develop the 55-ac Crocker Amazon reservoir site (PUC/Water Dept land)
planting_note: WPA built ballfields, bleachers and playground in 1930s; still being built out c.1940

name: Twin Peaks
start_event: City purchased the summits 1915 (park later grew to ~64 ac)
planting_note: Summits kept as grass/scrub; Sutro eucalyptus on lower slopes planted mid-1880s; Christmas Tree Point overlook 1985

name: Mt. Davidson Park
start_event: First 20 ac bought (purchase approved 1927); park dedicated 1929; +6 ac c.1934, +7 ac 1941, more 1950
planting_note: Forest planted on Adolph Sutro's land by schoolchildren/unemployed on first Arbor Days (from 1886); east slope left treeless

name: Bay View Park
start_event: Dedicated as a park 1915 (Burnham 1905 plan's 'Visitacion Park')
planting_note: Hill forested 1900-1940; WPA roadways and landscaping 1930s (1954 Planning report)

name: Buena Vista Park
start_event: Set aside 1867 as 'Hill Park' by Outside Lands committee; later renamed Buena Vista
planting_note: WPA paths with gutters of reused headstones 1930s

name: Sigmund Stern Recreation Grove
start_event: Donated to city by Rosalie Stern 1931; dedicated 4 Jun 1932
planting_note: Eucalyptus grove planted by the Greene family in 19th c.; WPA landscaping 1930s

name: Pine Lake Park
start_event: City bought lake and land within five years after Stern Grove opened in 1932 (exact year not found; range 1932-37)
planting_note: Eucalyptus around lake planted by Greene family (19th c.)

name: Bernal Heights Park
start_event: Rec & Park Commission voted 1972 to take hilltop from Public Works; transfer celebrated 10 Jun 1973; Prop J protection 1974
planting_note: Kept as open grassland; Bernal Heights Blvd ring road built 1935 (WPA)

name: Balboa Park
start_event: Dedicated 1909 on 100-ac House of Refuge lot (dedication ceremony 1910); western part given to City College 1936
planting_note: Development slowed by Ingleside Jail until 1934; forested 1900-1940 (1954 Planning report)

name: Interior Greenbelt
start_event: Purchased by the city in the 1950s (exact year not found; decade midpoint)
planting_note: Part of Sutro Forest: eucalyptus planted by Adolph Sutro from the 1880s; trail dates to 1880s

name: Lower Great Highway
start_event: Great Highway paved 1929 (1927 Boulevard Bond) with Lower GH service road east of old 1890s rail berm; Ocean Beach strip designated for public use in 1868 Outside Lands order
planting_note: O'Shaughnessy's Ocean Beach Esplanade completed 1928; median strip landscaped

name: Palace of Fine Arts
start_event: Built for 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition (opened Feb 1915); only structure kept on site
planting_note: Lagoon landscape from 1915; rotunda rebuilt in concrete 1964-74; lagoon renovated 2009

name: West Sunset Playground
start_event: Playground and co-located schools opened 1954 (land first proposed 1930, planning 1946)
planting_note: Landscape contract 1954

name: Park Presidio Blvd
start_event: Land purchased 1903 ($360,000) as extension of Golden Gate Park
planting_note: Grading and planting begun by 1910; widened and re-landscaped late 1930s as Golden Gate Bridge approach

name: Mission Dolores Park
start_event: City bought former Jewish cemeteries 1905 as 'Mission Park' (1903 ballot measure)
planting_note: Refugee camp 1906-08; planted terraces, tennis courts, athletic field by 1910

name: Louis Sutter Playground
start_event: Completed 1965 under McLaren Park 1959 master plan

name: St. Mary's Playground
start_event: WPA began shaping St. Mary's Recreation Area 1933 on former St. Mary's College land (subdivided 1924)
planting_note: WPA grading, rubble walls and landscaping 1933-34

name: Corona Heights
start_event: City purchased 16-ac Rock Hill 1941 ($27,333) and named it Corona Heights

name: Mountain Lake Park
start_event: 20 ac at Mountain Lake designated for a public park by Outside Lands committee (Order No. 800, 1868); Wikipedia gives c.1875 for Hall's design
planting_note: ~20,000 trees planted c.1890; WPA work 1930s; lake reduced by 1930s Park Presidio/MacArthur Tunnel fill

name: Alamo Square
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (Mayor Van Ness named it 1856; legislature confirmed 1858)
planting_note: Squatter evicted 1868; graded and landscaped with paths and walls 1892

name: Julius Kahn Playground
start_event: Playground named for Rep. Julius Kahn in 1926; on Presidio land under revocable federal permit (renamed Presidio Wall Playground 2019)
planting_note: WPA improvements 1930s

name: Midtown Terrace Playground
start_event: Not found. Built on covered Sutro Reservoir after Midtown Terrace subdivision (1953-60); RPD budgeted $160,000 in 1950s; listed in 1965-67 RPD report

name: Moscone Recreation Center
start_event: Reserved as Lobos Square in 1855 Western Addition plan; later Funston Playground; renamed for Mayor Moscone after 1978
planting_note: 1906 refugee camp; playfield developed 1920s; East Playground 2018

name: Alta Plaza Park
start_event: Reserved as 'Alta Square' by 1855 Van Ness Ordinances (title suit settled 1888)
planting_note: Graded, terraced, walled and planted 1890-92

name: India Basin/Shoreline Park
start_event: Phase 1 (paths, picnic areas, restored wetland) completed 1996
planting_note: Phase 2 trailside landscaping to 2005; 900 Innes expansion opened Oct 2024

name: Lafayette Park
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (confirmed 1858); Holladay lots inside bought 1935
planting_note: About half improved by 1910; fully built out by WPA 1936-38

name: Ocean View Playground
start_event: Not found. Land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); playground construction photo dated 1930
planting_note: Trees and lawns added 1930s

name: Potrero Hill Recreation Center
start_event: Not found. Existing 'Potrero Hill Playground' improved by WPA late 1930s; photographed 1940; in 1954 inventory

name: Parkside Square
start_event: Reserved as public square in Outside Lands Order No. 800 (1868 map)
planting_note: Developed under WPA in 1930s

name: Holly Park
start_event: Deeded to city 1862 per Bernalwood/Wikipedia (story of purchase by J.G. Fair is doubtful)
planting_note: Holly Park Circle road 1894; proper landscaping incl. eucalyptus 1926

name: Douglass Playground
start_event: Not found. Land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); in use by 1928, graded 1930
planting_note: WPA landscaping late 1930s

name: McCoppin Square
start_event: Reserved in Outside Lands Order No. 800 (1868 map); named for Mayor Frank McCoppin
planting_note: Landscaped with tennis courts and playground 1910s-20s

name: Golden Gate Heights Park
start_event: Land donated by Carl G. Larsen (appeared before Supervisors 30 Oct 1928, died a week later)
planting_note: Listed as 'Sunset Heights Park' in 1954; hilltop forested 1900-1940

name: George Christopher Playground
start_event: Opened 1971 as part of Diamond Heights redevelopment

name: Herz Playground
start_event: Completed 1965 (newly dedicated in FY1965-66)

name: Carl Larsen Park
start_event: Two blocks donated by Carl G. Larsen in early 1920s; Mayor Rolph honored the donation 4 Oct 1926

name: Angelo J. Rossi Playground
start_event: Not found. Grounds developed by WPA in 1930s (1954 Planning report); playground photos c.1930 before pool built
planting_note: WPA landscaping 1930s; lawns and trees noted in 1954

name: Youngblood-Coleman Playground
start_event: Housing site abandoned after 1974 accident; 'Galvez Playground Phase I (Youngblood-Coleman)' completed FY1977-78

name: Jefferson Square
start_event: Reserved in 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (Western Addition)

name: Silver Terrace Playground
start_event: Not found. Listed as 'Silver Terrace Playfield' in 1954 Planning inventory

name: Raymond Kimball Playground
start_event: Block cleared 1959-60 in Western Addition redevelopment for 'future Raymond Kimbell Playground' (official spelling Kimbell)
planting_note: Fieldhouse built FY1965-67; renovated 2015

name: Gilman Playground
start_event: WPA crews excavated and graded 'Gilman Beach Playground' Dec 1933-Jan 1934
planting_note: Rehabilitated and landscaped 1968

name: Franklin Square
start_event: Established 1868 per SF Parks Alliance (1954 Planning report says Potrero squares laid out with the 1850s Western Addition)
planting_note: Soccer field 1984

name: Margaret S.Hayward Playground
start_event: South half of Jefferson Square reserved 1855; given to Playground Commission 1907-24 and made a playground
planting_note: Renovated 2020

name: Palega Playground
start_event: Not found. Formerly Portola Playfield (renamed 1996); land bought by Supervisors for Playground Commission sometime 1907-1924 (1954 Planning report); photo 1935

name: Telegraph Hill/Pioneer Park
start_event: Hilltop donated and named Pioneer Park for the 1876 Centennial; later purchases enlarged it
planting_note: Coit Tower 1933

name: Hawk Hill
start_event: Not found. 4.5-ac dune-remnant natural area at 14th Ave and Rivera; not in 1954 Planning inventory

name: Aptos Playground
start_event: Playground Commission bought land over 3 years from FY1927-28 (1931 county history timeline)

name: Walter Haas Playground
start_event: Not found. Built in Diamond Heights redevelopment (1961-81); site graded c.1957-60

name: Joseph L. Alioto Performing Arts Piazza
start_event: Civic Center Plaza laid out with Civic Center (1912 bond; City Hall opened Dec 1915; Wikipedia infobox says 1911); renamed for Alioto 28 Oct 1998
planting_note: London plane allees; completed c.1925; rebuilt 1956-60 over Brooks Hall and garage

name: Jackson Playground
start_event: Opened to public 1912 on a reserved Potrero square

name: Potrero del Sol
start_event: Site cleared 1976; park under construction 1980 and called 'new' in 1981 (La Raza Park)
planting_note: Skatepark added 2008

name: Duboce Park
start_event: Van Ness Ordinance hospital-lot reservation dedicated as Duboce Park Sep 1900
planting_note: Built 1901-02

name: Ferry Park
start_event: Completed 1975 (Golden Gateway redevelopment); renamed Sue Bierman Park 2007
planting_note: Redesigned 2011

name: Justin Herman/Embarcadero Plaza
start_event: Completed and opened 1972 (Golden Gateway redevelopment); renamed Embarcadero Plaza 2017

name: Grand View Park
start_event: About an acre at the summit dedicated as parkland 1923; slope lots bought back mid-1970s
planting_note: Moraga St stairs built 1927

name: O'Shaughnessy Hollow
start_event: Acquired by eminent domain in the 1990s (exact year not found; decade midpoint)

name: South Sunset Playground
start_event: Not found. Listed in 1954 Planning inventory (40th Ave and Vicente)

name: Brooks Park
start_event: Brooks property (373 Ramsell St) bought FY1966-67 with HUD open-space grant as a natural park
planting_note: Existing trees pruned and labeled before opening

name: Billy Goat Hill
start_event: Officially became a city park 1975 (3.5 ac)

name: Union Square
start_event: Set aside as a public plaza 1850 (Mayor John Geary)
planting_note: Redesigned 2002

name: Washington Square
start_event: Designated a city square in Jasper O'Farrell's 1847 survey
planting_note: Columbus Ave cut through 1873-75; 1950s redesign with poplars

name: Portsmouth Square
start_event: Used as a public gathering place from 1833; set aside as official plaza 1835 (Plaza de Yerba Buena)

name: South Park
start_event: City took over the private oval park 1897 (laid out 1852-55 by George Gordon as private square)
planting_note: Private oval garden from 1855; renovated 2017

name: Collins P. Huntington Park
start_event: Huntington mansion site donated by Arabella Huntington 1915
planting_note: Tortoise fountain 1955

name: Sue Bierman Park
start_event: Same as RPD polygon 'Ferry Park': completed 1975, renamed Sue Bierman Park 2007
planting_note: Redesigned 2011

name: Monster Park
start_event: Candlestick Park stadium site, not a park: ground broken 1958, opened Apr 1960, named Monster Park 2004-08, last event Aug 2014, demolished by Sep 2015. start_year intentionally blank

name: Salesforce Park
start_event: Rooftop park opened 12 Aug 2018 (closed Sep 2018 - Jul 2019 for beam repairs)

name: Presidio forest
start_event: Army mass tree planting began on Arbor Day 1886 under Maj. W.A. Jones's March 1883 plan (Presidio became a park 1994)
planting_note: 329,975 trees planted by 1892; ~420 ac by 1901 (Monterey pine, cypress, eucalyptus)

name: Crissy Field
start_event: Restored marsh and shoreline park reopened 2001 (NPS and GG National Parks Conservancy)

name: Crissy Field airfield
start_event: Army accepted airfield 24 Jun 1921; closed to airplanes 1974

name: Yerba Buena Gardens
start_event: North block (Mission-Howard) opened 11 Oct 1993; south block opened 1998

name: Lands End
start_event: Became part of Golden Gate National Recreation Area (created 1972); land acquisitions continued into the 1970s
planting_note: Headlands treeless except willows until 1930s, then pine, eucalyptus and cypress planted

name: Sutro Heights
start_event: Sutro family gave estate to city 1938 as a free public park (Sutro opened gardens to public by 1883); city transferred to NPS 1976
planting_note: Gardens planted by Adolph Sutro from 1881-83
